public_comment.topic: Disappointed that school sports funding was not added to tonight's agenda as had been discussed at the last meeting.
Asked for a full accounting of music/chorus program cuts across the district and wants district staff and the Musicators booster president to identify fundraising priorities to fill gaps.

Urged the committee not to reopen this year's budget but instead to plan now, including requesting a special town meeting article, so it can act quickly if the state budget brings additional local aid.

public_comment.stated_role: chair of the parks commission, parent of two student athletes
public_comment.topic: Supported allowing athletes a PE credit/waiver, noted a softball playoff win, and raised the need for better field-scheduling coordination between the parks department and the schools for summer programming.

Raised difficulty scheduling summer programs early enough for families, and supported calling the proposed PE policy a 'credit' rather than a 'waiver,' offering to help collect sample policies from other districts.

budget_items.topic: Potential state local aid to Lunenburg
budget_items.what_was_said: A public commenter said the Senate budget could deliver additional local aid to Lunenburg depending on how it is calculated, and urged the committee to plan ahead for it.

budget_items.topic: Special town meeting article for possible state windfall
budget_items.what_was_said: A commenter urged the committee to ask the select board for a special town meeting in August with an article allowing the school department to receive any additional state funding.
The commenter said the committee could put additional funds to good use even though layoffs and staffing decisions are already underway.
The committee accepted a donation from Turkey Hill's PTO book fair sales.
Transfers were held over and not acted on this meeting; a budget check was also planned before June 30.

budget_items.topic: Booster club fundraising and Title IX
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said only the school committee may formally accept donations and that a booster club raising money for one team can obligate the district to fund an equal experience for the counterpart team under Title IX.

budget_items.topic: PE waiver equity concern - sports fee
budget_items.what_was_said: A committee member noted that families need to be able to pay a stated sports fee and provide transportation to be eligible for a proposed PE waiver, raising an equity concern.

Mr. Ballister's proposal would charge roughly a stated per-student amount for a before-school fifth grade band with a goal of about 20 students, said to be less than the cost of an instrument or private lessons.
The existing after-school program fee was cited as a comparison point, noted as insufficient on its own to cover a stipend for a similar program like the band proposal.
The superintendent noted a conference committee figure for statewide tutoring funding that the district might apply for again if eligible.

budget_items.topic: Ignite tutoring program cost per seat
budget_items.what_was_said: The cost of an Ignite tutoring seat was described as too expensive for the current budget even using Title I funds; this year's use was grant funded.
The facilities director reported switching maintenance vendors and locking in a three-year rate saved money compared to the prior separate contracts for the two buildings.

decisions.decision: Line-item transfers were deferred to the following week's meeting rather than acted on.
A public budget check will be done before June 30.
The PE credit/waiver proposal was not brought to a vote tonight because two members were absent; more information on peer districts will be gathered first.
The committee agreed to discuss district finances and whether to pursue another override or other funding request at the next meeting.
The upcoming meeting with athletic boosters will inform whether related items go on a future agenda.

minutes.headline: After the override's defeat, the committee agreed to weigh another override or funding request at its next meeting.
minutes.summary: The committee heard extensive public comment and its own remarks on the aftermath of the failed override, including a call to plan for possible state-aid windfalls via a special town meeting, but reached no formal decision beyond agreeing to revisit finances next meeting. It also tabled a proposed physical education credit/waiver for varsity athletes due to absent members, reviewed strong end-of-year academic testing and Ignite tutoring results, approved FY27 handbooks and a Turkey Hill donation, authorized negotiating a fifth-grade band stipend with the union, and accepted a facilities report citing maintenance-contract savings.

what_happened.line: After the override's defeat, the committee agreed to take up another override or funding request at its next meeting.
Line-item transfers were deferred to the following meeting, with a public budget check planned before June 30.
A proposed physical education credit or waiver for varsity athletes was tabled after two members were absent; the committee will gather information from peer districts first.
The committee voted unanimously to accept a Turkey Hill PTO donation and, later, the facilities and grounds report citing maintenance-contract savings.

The committee also took up FY27 school handbooks and authorizing the superintendent to negotiate a fifth-grade band stipend with the union, but the recording does not make the vote outcome on either audible.

why_it_matters: Another override vote or funding request may come back to residents, following the defeat of the prior one.
The deferred line-item transfers and the pre-June-30 budget check affect how the current fiscal year's school budget closes out.
The tabled PE credit/waiver would change graduation or scheduling requirements for varsity athletes if it comes back for a vote.
watch_next: Next School Committee meeting: discussion of district finances and whether to pursue another override or funding request
A public budget check before June 30, and action on the deferred line-item transfers

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the figures and votes both happened to capture — the state-aid range, the Turkey Hill donation, the band fee, and the facilities-report vote all match — but each record holds substantial material the other omits entirely: ours has no committee-member names, warrant totals, or public-comment detail, while the official minutes omit several dollar figures (tutoring grant, Ignite cost, after-school fee, custodial contract breakdown) discussed in reports. The one real fact-level split worth checking is the fifth-grade band motion: our recording describes it as authorizing the superintendent to negotiate a stipend with the union, while the official minutes describe a vote approving a $100/20-student before-school program — a different action on the same agenda item.
